request: Owner, /portal screenshot of the cabinet hero: «мотоциклский райд… в виде гифки будет очень плох. Либо через Хиксвилл сделай это видео и запускай просто как видео… переделай кадр… другую локацию, пусть он едет где-то там по Амальфи… сохраняя все пропорции… максимально бесшовно».
generation: Empty Amalfi coastal road, 4:3 (Higgsfield image, job 974e7810-a804-4647-8954-839f7c05da1d): the road across the lower third, sea and sky above, Positano-like village on the right, lemon tree and bougainvillea in front.
Vespi riding the same road as a reference (Higgsfield image, job f61f937b-6eb6-49fa-8cbe-0735dc5c62d3), Vespi identity from the three approved references.

Video (Higgsfield, job 2a0b9690-4723-41a7-931a-be5f4b37355c): start and end frame are the empty road, the riding still is the reference; 10 s, 4:3, 2176 × 1632, 24 fps, no audio. Vespi enters on the left at frame 42 and leaves on the right by frame 218.
diagnosis: The video frames are sharp, but the whole background drifts by about 1 px (median optical flow 0.4–1.4 px) and its first and last frames differ by 2.4/255 at the edges of every detail: a plain loop would twitch at the wrap and the shimmer costs bitrate (1600 px at CRF 22 came to 6 MB).
fix: Plate: one empty-road frame of the video (source frame 30), still for the whole loop.

Per frame, Vespi is found by his red helmet (saturated red where the plate has none); a box sized from the helmet (1.2 helmet heights behind, 1.55 ahead, 2.95 down) holds the convex hull of everything that differs from the plate by more than 30/255 after a 3 px blur — Vespi and his scooter, never the drifting background around him. Hull dilated 4 px, feathered 2.5 px.
His shadow on the road: a band under the wheels (up to 2.6 helmet heights ahead, the sun is behind him), taken where the frame is darker than the plate, soft.

Loop: source frames 34–220 with Vespi composited, then 18 frames of the plate; 205 frames, 8.54 s at 24 fps. Vespi is on screen 7.4 s, the empty road between rides 1.2 s. Frames without Vespi are the plate itself, so the wrap is exact (difference 0).
Encode: x264 slow, CRF 21 / 22 / 25 at 2176 / 1600 / 960, one keyframe (keyint 400, scenecut 0), BT.709 tags, faststart; VP9 960 CRF 36, g 400.
Posters landscapes/amalfi-{960,1600,2176}.webp: frame 72 of the loop (Vespi left of centre on the road), decoded with the BT.709 matrix, WebP q82. LivingLandscape starts at 72.5/24.
Proportions: 4:3 like the Tuscan scene (1600 × 1200 against 1600 × 1207); the hero keeps its tile, crop and object-position (50% 100%), the road and Vespi stay below the panel.

revision_same_day.request: Owner, iPad screenshot of /portal the same evening: «то, что на Амальфи всё ещё лагает, всё ещё это не работает».
diagnosis: The generated ride is 24 fps. On a 60 Hz screen (iPad, most laptops) 24 fps frames are held for 2 and 3 refreshes in turn, so a figure moving sideways judders; every other loop on the site is 30 fps.

Vespi's own speed in the generated ride is uneven: tracked by matching his helmet and face from frame to frame (sub-pixel peak), he rides 13 px a frame, slows to 9–10 px around source frames 140–150, then speeds up to 22 px a frame towards the exit (2176 px frame).
fix: Each source frame's Vespi is cut as before (helmet-anchored box, convex hull of what differs from the plate, soft edge, his shadow).

The loop is rebuilt at 30 fps with Vespi at one steady speed: every output frame takes the source frame whose Vespi is nearest to the position a steady ride needs and shifts that cut-out by the remaining distance (Lanczos, sub-pixel; vertical position follows the road's curve). While he is cut by the left or right edge of the picture, only shifts that move the cut edge out of the picture are allowed.

225 ride frames (source frames 37–216) and 30 frames of the still road: 255 frames, 8.5 s. Measured on the result by the same head matching: 11.0 px a frame, standard deviation 0.4 px (the generated ride: 9–22 px).
Same encode settings, now -r 30. Posters are frame 81 of the new loop; LivingLandscape starts at 81.5/30. A tablet (820 px wide, 2×) loads the 1600 px file.
revision_same_day.tools: scratchpad scripts track.py (head matching) and retime.py (cut-outs, steady 30 fps); not part of the site.
